What we say, drafted from: counts forward and back in steps; extends a sequence; says its rule
'forward/backward counting' is Cambridge's 'Count on and count back in steps of constant size … from 0 to 1000'.
'extending patterns, rules' is Cambridge's 'extend linear sequences, and describe the term-to-term rule'.
Ours extends counting sequences; NCF-SE also names odd, even and square numbers, powers of 2 and 10, and Virahanka–Fibonacci numbers.
Ours covers 'extends patterns in … numbers'; NCERT's patterns in shapes belong to Geometry.

The secondary capability LO-G3-0928 builds.

What we say, drafted from: reads numbers below zero; places them on a number line; orders positive and negative numbers
'ordering' negative numbers is Cambridge's 'compare and order positive and negative numbers, using the symbols =, > and <'.
'number lines' below zero are Cambridge's counting on and back 'extending beyond zero to include negative numbers'.
Ours reads numbers 'below zero'; Cambridge also asks for numbers 'greater than 1000', which LO-G3-0952 covers.
NCF-SE's Preparatory Stage (ages 8–11) does not ask for negative numbers; it brings in 'zero and negative quantities as numbers' in the Middle Stage (ncf.math.M.C-1.3, ages 11–14).

What we say, drafted from: reads and writes numbers; says what each digit is worth; partitions a number
'reading/writing large numbers' is Cambridge's 'read and write number names and whole numbers (from 0 to 1000)'.
Place value is Cambridge's 'the value of each digit is determined by its position in that number (up to 3-digit numbers)'.
'partitioning' is Cambridge's 'Compose, decompose and regroup 3-digit numbers, using hundreds, tens and ones'.
Ours reads, writes and partitions numbers to 1000; NCF-SE asks, across ages 8–11, for 'the Indian number system' and 'the names of very large numbers'.
Ours is NCERT's 'reads and writes numbers up to 999 using place value'; its adding, subtracting, tables and division sit in other objectives on this step.
